accounts.name: Roche (incl. Genentech/Diagnostics)

accounts.priority_reason: 1 open opportunity, 1 in the 2026-27 window, 1 with a Strong fit. Penzberg's EUR 600M+ diagnostics production centre is the single largest Roche investment in Germany and is mid-construction with commissioning 2027-28: a near-term automation/MES/validation entry point.

accounts.priority_reason: 3 open opportunities, 3 in the 2026-27 window, 2 with a Strong fit. Three concurrent capital projects at Visp/Stein with 2027-28 start-up dates, at a CDMO that buys automation and MES per suite.

gaps_html:
How this dashboard was built

Scope filter: accounts with no open opportunity were removed from this view on 7 Oct 2026, except Takeda, Merck KGaA, Sandoz, GSK, BioNTech, Pfizer and AstraZeneca, which were kept as opportunity accounts; 21 accounts and 16 site records were excluded.

This is a fresh research pass (7 Oct 2026) on the listed accounts using web search across company newsrooms, wire services, regional business and trade press, and state/cantonal investment agencies, in German and English. Each record carries source links and a confidence rating (High = company or official source; Medium = reputable trade or regional press; Low = single or undated/indirect source). The layout, filters, fit-matrix logic and record structure follow the US dashboard.

Known limitations — please read

  • Search-synthesis only. This build could not open primary documents (annual reports, press-release PDFs, Handelsregister, state-aid decisions). Facts come from search-result summaries and snippets, so most items are Medium/Low confidence and many dates are “Unverified”. Confirm before customer-facing use.
  • Reference files not available. The earlier DACH CSV/sources/territory plan, the earlier DACH dashboard, the corrected US CSV and the PowerPoint template were not in this build environment, so nothing from the earlier DACH research was reused and brand colours/fonts are taken from the US dashboard's CSS. The official Orise logo (black wordmark, inverted to white on the teal header) is embedded.
  • Currencies. Amounts are shown in the announcement currency (EUR, CHF; two Novartis items are announced in USD). The KPI row shows EUR, CHF and USD totals separately. Only the map shading by “Investment” converts to euro-equivalents using indicative planning rates of 1 CHF = 1.07 EUR and 1 USD = 0.86 EUR (set 7 Oct 2026, not live market rates); replace them in dach_data.py if needed.
  • Totals are a floor. 20 of 51 records have no disclosed amount; network programmes (e.g. Bayer >EUR 1.4B, Roche CHF 1.2B Basel programme) are not split across sites. Several records bundle older projects (pre-2024) kept for footprint context and marked Monitor / Closed.
  • Inferred figure. Lilly Alzey (EUR ~1.15B) is inferred as half of the original EUR 2.3B after a reported 2026 cut; confirm directly.
  • Greenfield vs brownfield. Greenfield = new stand-alone site or plant on previously undeveloped land; brownfield = new building, line or expansion at an existing site.
  • Opportunity status. Open = in design, build, commissioning or ramp-up with a clear automation/MES need; Monitor = completed, R&D/non-manufacturing or too early; Closed/late = completed before the window, or site closure. The “2026-27 window” flag marks projects with construction, commissioning or start-up in 2026-2027.
  • Tiers are computed: Tier 1 = at least one open opportunity in the 2026-27 window with a Strong fit; Tier 2 = other open opportunities or Monitor items with Moderate fit; Tier 3 = none identified. Fit ratings are analyst judgement from project scope, not confirmed buying intent. Incumbent vendors were not researched (empty).
  • Coordinates are city-level approximations.
  • Map. Equal-size tiles for 16 German Länder, 9 Austrian Bundesländer and 26 Swiss cantons (Liechtenstein: no site).

Ownership and structure checks

  • Sandoz is a standalone company since the Oct 2023 spin-off from Novartis; Hexal is a Sandoz subsidiary and its Holzkirchen record sits under Sandoz.
  • MSD is Merck & Co. (USA) outside North America, including Intervet/Animal Health, and is unrelated to Merck KGaA (Darmstadt; EMD in the US).
  • Catalent is owned by Novo Holdings (deal closed Dec 2024). BioNTech absorbed CureVac. Bode Chemie belongs to PAUL HARTMANN AG (bought from Beiersdorf). KBI Biopharma is a JSR company. Takeda acquired Shire/Baxalta plasma assets (Vienna, Linz).
